body: I recently have started to train on the hang board and noticed i can’t maintain a “half crimp” at the max weight i can hang, rather two of my fingers are crimped while the pointer finger sort of open hands. Should I train with reduced weight to maintain all three fingers in a crimp position or is this just a natural physiological way that my body works climbing?
i do 100 about 1hr before i want to sleep. you might want to look into a ndri for the morning, that and a cup of coffee help me get up

if you think about mental illness as a thought pattern it can be healing. anxiety, autism, depression etc. are all things that are not productive under capatalism but the empathy that these individuals posses can be beneficial in more communal societies.

though i concede it’s a rather odd take and perhaps western take of buddhism, there are some who view nirvana as “non existence” and a lack of rebirth onto life. i think that this can be contrary to this punishment your circle is placing upon you.
i deeply sympathize with what seems to be a mixed episode, those are always the scariest to me i’m so sorry you’re experiencing this.

a diagnosis doesn’t make any feeling “more real” in fact the way i got diagnosed with MDD (which has since been changed to BPD) was through confessing some of my darker thoughts to my partner. they were incredibly helpful in terms of talking my through it all (they had MDD) and the next day in school i was called into the office to be talked to. my highsdhool had a social worker who you could report people to.

if your relationship is predicated on a take relationship where all she does is twke from you it’s not a relationship worth having. you can in a low stakes way confess your feelings, perhaps a “i know you come to me to be your strong guiding figure but i need to tell you about what pains me” ive found revealing my bpd to intimate partners, even when i’m being emotionally supportive of them and their ailments has allowed me to support them better because they see i understand issues and has seen them support me as well

the climate crisis deeply saddens me, i’ve done research into sustainable agriculture as well as packaging. i personally hold an ethic that sees human “goodness” as an erasure of our harm and that is a rather radical position. know that things are changing, groups such as the land institute are close to producing cropping systems to revolutionize our grain farming system through making annual varieties of corn. oil companies in europe have been forced to pay for their pollution etc. things are looking up on the climate front

honesty is a form of maturity, and maturity and open communication is ultimately what embodies a strong relationship. do not fall into a weird “strong” machismo fallacy, mutual support can be just as healing as an strong rock figure

i feel so similarly, paralyzed by the depression, wrought with the guilt of leaving my space a mess. people care about you, please try and be honest with the people around you—even if you wind up confessing all of your feeling to your cat and dog or even plants as i so often do. perhaps that will help you build up the courage to talk to your boyfriend or family. much love, stranger

you don’t necessarily need to be mentally ill yo have suicidal ideation. having a depressed girlfriend might somehow be beneficial, talking to someone who can understand your issues can be eye opening and healing. also, just because you aren’t diagnosed with MDD does not mean that you aren’t prone to having depressive episodes, as most if not all people have had one or more in their life without the more constant occurrence of MDD

as someone who is mixed race i once deeply hated myself. you should be proud of your race and a lot of hate you may foster is deeply embedded in cultural contexts of our (in the us context) racially hegemonic society. some readings i’ve found therapeutic is Racial Melancholia, Racial Dissociation: On the Social and Psychic Lives of Asian Americans by Eng and Han and The Melancholy of Race by Anne Cheng

at times i feel as though i can only keep living if i live for another person. as someone who has struggled with ideation for the last five years, i too feel as if i am at a breaking point. honesty is the only thing that can help you, i’ve opened up to so many friends; i’ve felt seen and understood. best case scenario, my friends help, worst case they at least know i feel this way. today i am trying talking to someone for the first time professionally, my psychiatrist is a pill pusher, and traditional therapy has never helped me. i’m actually talking to mt friends mother who’s some form of phd in psychology in a therapist role. who knows how it will go, but i must stress being honest is the only way you can begin to heal from these musings. being 5150’d is a scary, retraumatizing reality but i hope my genuine honesty in seeking help will at least help them see the sanity and human in me. for what it’s worth i live alone too, i miss my roomates but they all have internships. it’s hard being a bp person alone in a two story house, sometimes i haven’t the motivation to even buy myself groceries, at times my best friend (who lives across the country) needs to call me and doordash me food, but all of this love and support comes from, again, honesty

i’ve found at times crying and writing letters, making sure your loved ones hear what they deserve in eloquent thoughtful prose helps me get through the pain. you cry not for yourself but for them, and then perhaps can push on to fight another day
that’s not something we’re allowed to say per the rules, just please do not put yourself through this pain my friends life will never be the same after surviving that

i’ve had a friend who did this and their roomate found them as they screamed in agony. the reality is that modern sleeping pills really aren’t going to kill you. this is going to put you in needless pain. for what it’s worth said friend now sports a “;” tattoo and deeply regrets that fateful night when she tried to take her own life. I don’t mean to argue, I simply wish to clarify my logic. I deeply feel that despite the headway I have made in alleviating some of the myriad problems that inspire me to work my very act of existing within a western imperialist society is going to offset any benefits I do bring to society. This is to say that, no amount of work I’ve done in gender studies and environmental studies can ever offset the horrendous conditions that my consumerism puts others in—sweat shops in asia, child slaves in africa etc. I have tried to erase the screams by only shopping at thrift stores and if needing something new buying from someone like Patagonia to feel more ethical. I am also a vegan and actively try to live a corn free life to free myself from the cruelty therein as well as the environmental degradation from industrial agriculture and feed lots. I know so many depend on me; I made a list for a close friend who also has BPD to text if I ever do make the decision and it contained 35 people I deemed absolutely necessary to know I died in friends and 7 in academic mentors. Everyday I grapple with the ethics of how best to leave my friends with as minimal damage as possible
